comments.body:
## Final evaluation — commit 24917e843b1472adc682bcde7a9c2e5a1727acfd

Overall verdict: unusually mature and well-governed for a project of this size. The dominant risks are localized complexity, incomplete type precision, and small documentation/test-environment truth gaps—not systemic correctness or testing weakness.

Ratings:
- Code quality: 7.5/10
- Architectural quality: 8.0/10
- Documentation quality: 8.0/10
- Test quality: 8.5/10

### Verification and measurements
- Ruff check + format-check passed across 1,831 files.
- Complexity ratchet passed: active=68, new=0, increased=0, stale=0.
- Mypy passed all 440 source modules.
- Zizmor, actionlint, documentation index/internal-link checks passed.
- Source inventory: 441 Python files, 131,246 LOC, median 229 LOC.
- Test inventory: 1,249 Python files, 265,045 LOC, 9,748 statically defined test functions: 7,565 unit; 1,333 interface/contract; 599 scripts; 158 integration; 81 external; 12 E2E.
- Canonical default suite after locked dependency sync, outside the socket-restricted sandbox: 11,480 passed, 19 skipped, 2 failed in 13m54s. Coverage was 83.86% combined, 85.77% statements, 78.19% branches.
- Integration lane: 138 passed, 1 skipped in 2m38s.
- No literal assert True tests found. Only 11 tests had exclusively weak local is-not-None-style assertions; sampled cases generally had meaningful surrounding behavioral setup/oracles.

### Strengths
1. Code/governance: shrink-only module-size, complexity, and typing ratchets; broad blocking Ruff/mypy/format gates; explicit environment/bootstrap policy; strong error and concurrency documentation.
2. Architecture: event ownership and adapters are clearly explained; CLI, library, and MCP share a core; selected high-risk seams have executable negative controls. The Jira-family boundary test includes synthetic forbidden edges, so it cannot pass vacuously.
3. Documentation: audience-oriented index, architecture + ADR corpus, generated CLI/MCP/env references, README golden path, internal-link/index gates, and roughly 1% measured duplicate lines. Context is generally layered rather than repeated.
4. Tests: unusually strong tiering and hygiene infrastructure. tests/conftest.py:95+ confines external markers and tests/conftest.py:149+ blocks accidental sockets; tests/interfaces/conftest.py:40 builds one isolated reusable store template per xdist worker; tests/external/conftest.py:121 fails an all-skipped live lane and :143 requires explicit opt-in. The weekly external matrix covers Anthropic, Bedrock, OpenAI, Jira Cloud, Jira Data Center, and Langfuse. Existing mutation documentation distinguishes behavioral tests from structural tripwires/change detectors and records 99–100% mapped scores on selected cores.

### Findings and remedies
MEDIUM-HIGH — Complexity/file-size debt. 87 source modules exceed the documented 500-LOC target (docs/architecture.md:299); llm/runner.py, _config_schema.py, and _commands/init.py are exactly 800 LOC, _ref_lock.py is 799, and signing.py is 798. Independent lizard analysis found 206 functions above complexity 15. Representative hotspots are compute() in src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py:96, which combines resolution, replay, BFS, tombstones, dependency readiness, parent policy, and greedy scheduling, and import_tickets() in src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py:118, a five-pass importer in one long orchestration function. Continue the existing shrink-only ratchets, prioritizing high-complexity orchestration and near-cap files; split only at current call-graph seams. The ratchet itself is a major strength and already prevents regression.

MEDIUM — Broad but shallow typing. Normal mypy passes all source, but a diagnostic global --disallow-untyped-defs run found 687 errors. pyproject.toml:462 globally ignores missing imports and only rebar.graph.* / rebar.grounding.* currently disallow untyped definitions (:504). Expand package-by-package strictness and narrow ignore_missing_imports at transport boundaries. Existing open ticket 06e0-fb68-657a-4ea1 tracks this direction.

MEDIUM — Architectural enforcement is selective rather than systemic. High-risk seams have good bespoke checks, but there is no small repository-wide package dependency/DAG contract, so new cross-layer imports outside protected families rely on review. Define stable layer contracts with positive and synthetic-negative controls while preserving facade/lazy-import exceptions. Follow-up: 44ea-43c6-b351-4d81.

MEDIUM — Assignee examples contradict reconciler behavior. README.md:44 and docs/user-guide.md:115 teach --assignee alice, while docs/config.md:431 requires an email/accountId and explains that a bare handle is left unassigned. Omit the option in quickstarts or use a clearly Jira-resolvable value. Included in 879f-5549-91e3-4d6f.

LOW — Documentation/navigation drift. docs/README.md:25 routes “Drive rebar over MCP” to llm-framework.md rather than mcp-reference.md; docs/README.md:91 describes removed .rebar/config.conf instead of rebar.toml/[tool.rebar]. .github/workflows/_optionality.yml:74+ still says core has only PyYAML and describes jsonschema as absent although the current dependency topology differs. pyproject.toml:457+ calls non-core mypy advisory despite the whole-library CI gate. Fix the source text and protect stable truths with deterministic drift checks. Follow-up: 879f-5549-91e3-4d6f.

LOW-MEDIUM — Mutation evidence is strong but stale/non-gating. docs/mutation-testing.md:92 and :110 date the recorded scores to June/July 2026, and no workflow invokes mutmut. Add a bounded scheduled/manual lane for only the already selected cores, failing on score regression/new survivors. Follow-up: 521b-04c3-572f-4514.

LOW — Two reproducible test-environment assumptions. tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py:142 recursively decodes every file under src/rebar as UTF-8, so an ignored Mach-O esbuild binary under editor_assets/node_modules fails the “shipped surfaces” check. tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:430 clones the audit checkout and fails when that checkout is a shallow promisor clone missing historical objects. The first test should enumerate tracked/package-shipped textual inputs; the second should use a self-contained Git fixture or explicitly handle partial checkouts. Both should retain negative controls so their behavioral oracles remain strong. Follow-up: def1-9c3c-6802-48bd.

### Limits
No live third-party calls were made because provider/Jira credentials were not in scope; external-integration quality is assessed from the tests, explicit opt-in/all-skipped controls, and scheduled workflow matrix rather than a live run. The independent complexity scan is diagnostic; the checked-in shrink-only ratchet is the authoritative gate. No production or test files were modified.

Related prior audit: 1d3c-547d-f0cf-426c.

## CI evidence addendum — GitHub Actions inspected 2026-08-08

The live CI record strengthens the external-integration assessment but exposes a material reliability flaw in the default-suite gate.

### Audited SHA / quality-gate status
- Gerrit Verified run 31269824243 on base SHA 24917e843b1472adc682bcde7a9c2e5a1727acfd succeeded across lint+type-check, pip-audit, artifact provenance, optional-dependency isolation, eval discipline, clean-install golden path, authorship identity, Ubuntu Python 3.11/3.12/3.13, and macOS Python 3.13.
- Its Ubuntu Python 3.11 cell ran 11,462 passed / 66 skipped at 83.49% coverage, plus 129 passed / 10 skipped in the integration tier.
- Recent CodeQL SAST: 5/5 green. Optional-Dependency Isolation mirror: 5/5 green. Recent Mirror Guard and Reconciler Heartbeat runs are green. Reconcile Bridge scheduled cancellations are concurrency supersession alongside successful dispatch runs, not job failures.

### Live external evidence
Latest complete Live External Integration run 30986591446 succeeded with zero skipped jobs:
- Jira Data Center: 62 passed, 1 xfailed; live canary executed 62/63 collected.
- Jira live-services/Cloud lane: 17 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed; live canary executed 8/9.
- Anthropic: 15 passed, 1 skipped; 15/16 live tests executed.
- Bedrock: 16 passed; 16/16 live tests executed.
- OpenAI: 15 passed, 1 skipped; 15/16 live tests executed.
- Langfuse round-trip: 1 passed.
This converts the original external-integration conclusion from workflow-design evidence to observed live execution evidence.

### New material finding
MEDIUM — CI gate reliability: the Python 3.11 xdist worker repeatedly dies in tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted with “node down: Not properly terminated,” after roughly 11.4k passing tests. Observed in Gerrit Verified runs 31266912051, 31267701635, 31268737675, and 31269084668, plus scheduled mirror runs 31245335199 and 31258682512. The identical Gerrit 1548 patchset then passed unchanged in run 31269824243, proving flakiness rather than patch behavior. Impact is a spurious Verified-1 and approximately 8–24 minutes of rerun latency per occurrence. Existing open ticket fade-ea90-7564-4715 already tracks the exact failure and proposed teardown/serialization investigation.

Revised test-quality score: 8.0/10 (from 8.5). External coverage and oracle design are excellent; repeatability of the blocking gate is currently below the same standard. Code 7.5, architecture 8.0, and documentation 8.0 remain unchanged.

## Context
Evaluate the current rebar repository for code quality, architectural quality, documentation quality (discoverability, understandability, and context efficiency), and test quality (behavioral, contractual, and external-integration coverage; avoidance of vacuous/change-detector tests; shared fixtures; and test hygiene). This is a read-only assessment; do not modify production or test files.

## Plan
- Map the implementation and package boundaries, dependency directions, public interfaces, state ownership, and high-complexity hotspots.
- Sample representative production paths for correctness, cohesion, readability, typing, error handling, and maintainability.
- Trace the documentation entry points, indexes, cross-links, generated references, architecture/ADR coverage, contributor guidance, and duplicated context.
- Inventory and sample unit, interface/contract, integration, property, golden, snapshot, subprocess, and external-service tests; inspect fixture reuse, isolation, determinism, assertions, skips, and CI execution.
- Run read-only repository quality gates and targeted test-collection/coverage diagnostics where safe.
- Report evidence-backed strengths and prioritized findings with exact citations, confidence, and remediation guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The report assesses code quality with evidence and representative citations.
- [x] The report assesses architectural boundaries, dependency direction, cohesion, and extension surfaces with evidence.
- [x] The report assesses documentation discoverability, understandability, accuracy signals, and context efficiency with evidence.
- [x] The report assesses behavioral, contractual, and external-integration test coverage with evidence.
- [x] The report assesses vacuous/change-detector risk, fixture reuse, isolation, determinism, and test hygiene with evidence.
- [x] Material findings have a severity, impact explanation, and concrete remedy.
- [x] The final evaluation distinguishes verified observations from sampling limits and records conclusions on this ticket.
